blindSummary: Public visibility under municipal pressure: one cancelled Pride, plus one department with a measured high offence rate. (1) 13 June 2026: the Pride march in a city of this state/province was cancelled because no volunteers could be found to staff its security — organisers: "we're talking about freedom, about love, about a space where you can be whoever you want" — in a city governed by a mayor whose record of bending public-space rules for conservative ends is separately documented (a human-rights league asked the senior state-appointed administrator to enforce a century-old secularism statute after municipal religious ceremonies). (2) A department of this state/province recorded 40 anti-LGBT offences in 2024 — 8.14 per 100,000 — about 6th-highest departmental rate in the country, per local analysis of interior-ministry statistics, in a department where attractive coastal cities coexist with conservative rural areas. The state/province also holds large openly-LGBT populations around its main university cities. National context from this record's sources: trans detainees in prisons are placed by the gender on their identity documents (criminal-procedure provisions) and fall into a legal grey area, punished beyond their alleged crimes — the national detention oversight body says transgender detainees "suffer the most" in detention; its 2021 Opinion (all places of deprivation of liberty; ~40 referrals since 2010) finds serious violations persist, with isolation, untrained staff and unimplemented 2016 depathologisation named as structural causes.
blindSourceSummaries: Investigative feature (Jan 2018) on transgender women in prisons: by law, placement follows the gender on identity documents (criminal-procedure provisions), so trans women legally marked male are held in all-male facilities — a case of three days in a men's facility near a major city after transfer in 2014, shouted at and threatened by inmates; another held under notorious conditions after a 2016 protest trial; the national detention oversight body states transgender detainees are the group that "suffers the most" in prison.

National detention oversight body's Opinion of 25 May 2021 on the treatment of transgender persons in all places of deprivation of liberty: serious violations persist across institutions (based on ~40 referrals since 2010 plus interviews and inspections); recommends that detained people choose the gender of their search officer and ward, no isolation because of trans identity, no dedicated trans-only wards, and ongoing hormone/medical care; extends to intersex and non-binary people; notes the 2016 depathologising law has not been translated into prison rules.

International anti-torture body interview with the national detention mechanism (May 2023) about its 2021 Opinion: trans persons in detention face constant risk of violence, discrimination and abuse; research found a lack of data on trans detainees' numbers and locations, almost no staff training, and no guidance implementing the 2016 law; central recommendation is that detaining authorities ask people what they require and respond; five dedicated inspection visits were carried out across regions and institution types.
blindTangential: The Pride cancellation is an anti-Pride hostility event affecting the whole local LGBTQIA+ community rather than gender expression specifically, but it removes the region's public visibility event and signals a hostile municipal climate that gender-nonconforming visitors would encounter in daily interactions.
